decision: Do not promote the published R-ev WALLET AC/DC/HPC grid as direct CPO/ad-hoc pricing for IT*ENB. R-ev is both an eMSP/interoperability service and an ENB-linked charging brand; the published app terms explicitly cover public charging points compatible with the app, including interoperable non-R-ev stations. Therefore the WALLET grid is an eMSP/app tariff unless a deterministic first-party proof ties it to direct/ad-hoc charging on IT*ENB EVSE.
positiveEvidence: Current R-ev terms publish WALLET 0.65/0.85/0.89 EUR/kWh by AC/DC/HPC class.
R-ev app terms state the service covers public charging stations compatible with the app, directly or via third parties.
R-ev App Store description explicitly says charging is possible at non-R-ev stations participating in interoperability.
R-Gruppo company profile links EnerBroker to the R-ev brand and charging-infrastructure activity.
Roaming-network documentation maps R-ev to IT-ENB, corroborating the identity linkage but not proving direct CPO tariff equivalence.
negativePaths: Published WALLET grid cannot by itself be treated as direct CPO/ad-hoc IT*ENB pricing because it is an app/eMSP tariff surface with roaming scope.
Third-party eMSP tariffs for R-ev/ENB are corroboration only and must not be promoted.
blockingCondition: Obtain deterministic IT*ENB EVSE -> direct/ad-hoc price evidence from QR/payment surface, direct station backend, PUN tariff payload, or first-party statement explicitly applying a tariff to ENB-operated/R-ev-owned stations independently of roaming/eMSP pricing.

set.blockingCondition: deterministic direct/ad-hoc IT*ENB tariff evidence; R-ev WALLET grid is eMSP/app scope and must remain separate

history: 2026-09-22: corrected channel classification after recrossing first-party R-ev app terms and interoperability scope; no tariff extrapolation.
